```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(SEAC)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
```

# Introduction

SEAC performs a KD-tree BLADE mask and a general MaxMin gene-set spatial co-localization analysis for Visium HD. Capture-boundary and non-tissue positions are KD-tree seeds; bins whose nearest seed has Euclidean distance at most one are excluded.

The published BLADE project also includes slide-level artefact tests. SEAC documents its narrower local KD-tree HD mask rather than claiming to implement those additional methods.

# A small SpatialExperiment

```{r toy-data}
counts <- rbind(
    A = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L),
    B = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L)
)
colnames(counts) <- paste0("bin", 1:8)
coords <- expand.grid(array_row = 1:4, array_col = 1:2)
spe <- SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(coords, row.names = colnames(counts)),
    spatialCoordsNames = c("array_col", "array_row")
)
sets <- list(left = "A", right = "B")
```

# Score and test a prefiltered toy object

```{r score-and-test}
scored <- maxMinScore(spe, sets)
head(as.data.frame(colData(scored)))

out <- tempfile("seac-permutation-")
tested <- maxMinPermutationTest(
    scored, sets,
    n_permutations = 10L,
    chunk_size = 5L,
    output_dir = out,
    seed = 1L
)
head(loadSEACResults(out))
```

# Space Ranger data

For a standard Space Ranger Visium HD output, call `runBladeQC()` yourself
with its root, `outs`, or a `square_XXXum` path. It saves a HDF5-backed
`SpatialExperiment`, a complete audit mask, and a JSON manifest. Review the
saved QC output before starting the permutation stage. The permutation
function reads the saved object; it never applies BLADE automatically.

Gene sets can contain Ensembl feature IDs or 10x gene symbols. SEAC resolves
the latter from `rowData(qc)$Symbol`, including every feature row that shares a
requested symbol.

```{r spaceranger, eval=FALSE}
gene_sets <- list(
    Paneth = c("LYZ", "DEFA5"),
    Goblet = c("MUC2", "CLCA1")
)

qc_dir <- "sample_SEAC_post_qc"
qc <- runBladeQC(
    input_dir = "/path/to/spaceranger-output",
    output_dir = qc_dir,
    bin_size = "016"
)

# The BLADE mask is saved at file.path(qc_dir, "blade_mask.h5").
# The post-QC object is saved at file.path(qc_dir, "spe").
# This call may be made in a later R session.
tested <- maxMinPermutationTest(
    x = qc_dir,
    gene_sets = gene_sets,
    output_dir = "sample_SEAC_permutation",
    n_permutations = 20L,
    chunk_size = 5L
)

post_qc <- HDF5Array::loadHDF5SummarizedExperiment(
    file.path(qc_dir, "spe")
)
results <- loadSEACResults("sample_SEAC_permutation")
```

Twenty permutations are useful only as a quick workflow smoke test. Use the
default 5,000 or another justified value for a formal analysis.

The upstream VisHD pipeline supports within-sample and pooled-sample
permutations. In SEAC, use `mode = "within"` (default) or `mode = "pooled"`
with a named list of saved QC directories. The `legacy_hotspot` result uses
the upstream lower-tail rank rule, while `fdr_significant` is an additional
BH-adjusted test. A within-sample result for a given sample and seed is
unchanged when other samples are added to the input list or reordered.
Previously saved SEAC 0.99.1 within-sample checkpoints use a different seed
scheme and must be restarted in a new output directory; pooled checkpoints
are unchanged.

# Relation to the Python VisHD pipeline

The [October 2026 VisHD update](https://github.com/KummerfeldLab/VisHD/commit/6eafca6c45c8d6f1b28016b117bc851a1ea9cc53)
added a per-sample permutation option alongside pooled permutations. SEAC's
`within` and `pooled` modes correspond to these two null models. The R
implementation draws category labels over UMI slots without expanding a long
table of every UMI; it preserves the same category and bin totals. Within a
sample, the seed for a permutation no longer depends on its position in a
multi-sample list.

The [later KDTree update](https://github.com/KummerfeldLab/VisHD/commit/4da1eaa3fd957bd34f5d3a9793cf623700637339)
parallelized Python nearest-neighbor queries without changing the MaxMin
definition. SEAC uses exact RANN queries and can parallelize independent
permutation blocks through `BPPARAM`. Its HDF5 output contains per-bin
`legacy_hotspot` calls equivalent to applying the upstream lower-tail rank
threshold, plus Monte Carlo p-values and BH-adjusted results. The Python
pipeline also creates annotated images; SEAC does not currently produce
those images.

# Reproducibility

The test stores a manifest and block checkpoints. Re-run the same call with the same output directory and `resume = TRUE` to continue an interrupted job. The random seed is assigned per permutation, so results do not depend on how the 5,000 iterations are chunked.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
